conventions.convention: The parameter set is nonempty. Confidence procedures require measurable membership sections for each fixed parameter; no sigma-algebra or joint measurability on the parameter set is required. Confidence level is the infimum of pointwise coverage probabilities.
A pivot is a family of measurable parameter-indexed maps with a common pushforward probability law; parameter measurability and parameter invertibility are not required.
Exact pivot coverage requires the actual measurable acceptance set to have mass 1−α. Closed quantile intervals retain endpoint atoms.
Test inversion uses measurable acceptance events on the full observation space, including realized auxiliary randomization, with the corresponding point-null acceptance probability at least 1−α.

The unknown-variance normal example assumes AC, n≥2, positive variance, and 0<α<1. It restricts all sampling laws to the common full-measure Borel space D_n={s>0}, and treats each variance as fixed while inverting the mean.
The uniform example assumes n≥1 and θ>0; the confidence interval is intersected with (0,∞), including for observations outside the sampling support.
The binomial model includes p=0 and p=1 with 0^0=1. Lower-tail rejection uses the strict inequality F_p(X)<α, so acceptance includes equality. U_n=1.

load_bearing.statement: A confidence-set procedure is a map C:X→P(Θ), for nonempty Θ, whose membership section C_η={x:η∈C(x)} is measurable for every η. Its coverage at θ is P_θ(C_θ), and its confidence level is inf_θ P_θ(C_θ).
For an experiment with nonempty Θ and a measurable space (S,Sigma), a family of measurable maps q_θ:X→S is a pivot if its pushforward law is the same probability measure ν for every θ∈Θ.

For an experiment with nonempty Θ, a pivot q_θ with common law ν, and measurable B, define C(x)={θ∈Θ:q_θ(x)∈B}. If ν(B)≥1−α, C has coverage at least 1−α. If ν(B)=1−α, coverage is exactly 1−α at every parameter value.

For an experiment on the full observation space with nonempty Θ and 0≤α≤1, let each A_η be a measurable point-null acceptance event, including any auxiliary randomization, with Q_η(A_η)≥1−α. Then C(y)={η∈Θ:y∈A_η} is a confidence set with coverage at least 1−α.

The normal examples depend on the candidate parameter. Clarify this sentence as a parameter-indexed measurable quantity; the formal definition and inversion arguments are sound.
